title: SQL: SECURITY DEFINER function exposes a caller-controlled key/column parameter to untrusted callers
why: Function submit_consent runs with elevated (SECURITY DEFINER) privileges, its EXECUTE grant reaches untrusted callers (authenticated, service_role), and it accepts caller-controlled key/column/path-shaped text parameter(s) 'p_evidence_path' with no allowlist guard. A caller can steer which field/path the definer writes or reads, turning the RPC into an arbitrary-field overwrite (real incident: PR #322's merge_analysis_payload_key accepted any payload key; fixed only after external review).
fix: Either (a) drop the caller-controlled parameter(s) entirely, (b) hard-allowlist the permitted values inside the function body (e.g. IF p_evidence_path NOT IN ('allowed_key') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION), and/or (c) REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, authenticated, public and grant only to service_role.
